title: ～こと — must ～ (written rule or instruction)
summary: Used at the end of a sentence after the dictionary or ない form to state a rule, notice or instruction: ～すること, ～しないこと. It is written-style and close to a command.

body.p: Often seen on notices at schools, workplaces and facilities, and in memos and instructions. The action is nominalized and placed at the end: 廊下を走らないこと, 提出日は守ること. It sounds objective and rule-like compared with ～しなさい.
Speaking this way to a superior is usually rude, though teachers or parents may say it to children or students. A prohibition with ～ないこと is more businesslike than ～てはいけません.

examples.ja: 廊下（ろうか）を走（はし）らないこと。
examples.tr: Do not run in the hallway.

examples.ja: 図書館（としょかん）では静（しず）かにすること。
examples.romaji: Toshokan de wa shizuka ni suru koto.

examples.ja: 締（し）め切（き）りは必（かなら）ず守（まも）ること。
examples.tr: Be sure to meet the deadline.

pitfalls: Used toward a superior it becomes a command and is rude. Use ～てください for requests.
Do not add です after the sentence-final こと.
